name: Cucuteni–Trypillia culture
capital: No capital (mega-sites such as Talianki and Maidanetske)
summary: A Copper Age farming culture of Moldova, Ukraine and Romania whose “mega-sites” of up to 46,000 people were among the largest settlements in the world in the 5th–4th millennia BCE.

location.value: From the Carpathian Mountains to the Dniester and Dnieper rivers (Moldova, western Ukraine, north-eastern Romania).

terrain.value: Fertile black-earth forest-steppe and river valleys.
terrain.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

climate.value: Temperate continental, with fertile black-earth soils.
climate.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

resources.value: Rich soil, timber, clay; copper from the Balkans.
resources.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

disasters.value: Climate change late in its history may have strained farming.
disasters.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

population.value: Its peak population may have reached or exceeded one million people.

urbanisation.value: Mega-sites with up to 3,000 structures and possibly 20,000–46,000 people (c. 4100–3500 BCE).

disease.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

migration.value: Late in its history, steppe peoples moved into the region.
migration.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

economicBase.value: Farming of wheat and barley, cattle, pigs and sheep.
economicBase.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

tradeRoutes.value: Copper and salt exchange with the Balkans.
tradeRoutes.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

wealth.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

moneyAndTax.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

inequality.value: Thought to have started fairly equal, with rising inequality linked to its downfall.

governmentType.value: No known state; possibly councils of households.
governmentType.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

keyRulers.value: No rulers are known; there was no writing.
keyRulers.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

succession.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

institutions.value: Large assembly houses in the mega-sites.
institutions.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

eliteConflict.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

armyAndTech.value: Little evidence of warfare; some settlements had ditches.
armyAndTech.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

majorWars.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

territoryChange.value: Spread across present-day Romania, Moldova and Ukraine, about 350,000 km².

alliancesRivals.value: Contacts with steppe herders to the east.
alliancesRivals.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

inventions.value: Copper working; planned settlements in rings.
inventions.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

scienceEducation.value: No writing; skilled pottery and kiln technology.
scienceEducation.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

openness.value: Contact with Balkan farming cultures and steppe peoples.
openness.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

religion.value: Female figurines and the deliberate burning of houses, probably as a ritual.
religion.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

languageWriting.value: No writing; the language is unknown.
languageWriting.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

artsArchitecture.value: Pottery painted with spirals in red, white and black.

socialStructure.value: Households and communities, with little sign of rich elites.
socialStructure.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

sharedIdentity.value: Shared pottery styles and house building.
sharedIdentity.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

neighbours.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

ideasReligions.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

colonisation.source: Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)

riseSignals.value: Emerged around 5050 BCE from earlier farming groups.

peakPeriod.value: The middle phase (about 4100–3500 BCE), with “mega-sites” of perhaps 10,000 people or more.

declineSignals.value: Rising inequality has been proposed as a cause of decline.

outcome.value: Faded around 2950 BCE, as steppe peoples spread and settlements shrank.

overallCertainty.value: Medium; mega-site populations are debated. Second source: Wikidata gives c. 5400–2650 BCE; Wikipedia’s lead gives c. 5050–2950 BCE.

knownFor.label: Mega-settlements
knownFor.note: Huge ring-shaped towns, among the largest of their time.

knownFor.label: House burning
knownFor.note: Settlements were deliberately burned, possibly as ritual.
